clue.text: Old hill indicated by black pointer

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an arrow is a sign that points the way

explanation.surface: An ancient hill is marked out by a dark signpost.
explanation.walkthrough: A barrow is an ancient burial mound, hence an 'old hill'.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is a prehistoric earth mound raised over graves, a man-made hill of antiquity.

clue.text: Wearing this, chaps are less likely to kiss

definitions.text: Wearing this, chaps are less likely to kiss

parts.words: Wearing this, chaps are less likely to kiss
parts.note: chaps here are not men but cracks in the skin of the lips; the ointment that prevents them is the answer

explanation.surface: Men wearing some item become less inclined to kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chaps' reads as men, but it is the verb or noun for chapped skin: wearing lip balm, your lips are less likely to chap.
explanation.definitionFit: Balm smeared on the mouth protects against cracked, sore skin, so chapping is less likely.

clue.text: Papers held up — around 5 PM on one occasion

indicators.note: the reversed papers go around the answer to the cross-referenced clue
in a down clue, held up means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ID is short for identity papers
the answer to 5 Down, a republic

explanation.surface: Documents raised around five in the afternoon on a particular day.
explanation.walkthrough: '5 PM' looks like a time of day, but 5 is the cross-reference to 5 Down and PM is the definition's prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British prime minister, leading the government in two separate terms.

clue.text: Club penguin, say, catching end of finger

indicators.note: the diver holds the final letter inside itself

parts.note: a penguin is an example of a diving bird, a diver

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A golf club's penguin mascot gets its fingertip caught.
explanation.walkthrough: A driver is the golf club used to hit off the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the driver is the long-hitting wooden club, one of the set of clubs.

clue.text: Republic in 3 scrapping borders

indicators.note: throwing away the edges means the first and last letters of that answer are dropped

parts.note: the answer to 3 Down, the Victorian prime minister

explanation.surface: A republic within a third region loses its frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a Middle Eastern state governed as a parliamentary republic.

clue.text: Mouse getting titchy bits of cheese after nibbling container

parts.note: Jerry is the mouse of the Tom and Jerry cartoons

indicators.note: the tiny pieces taken are the opening letters of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A cartoon mouse takes tiny crumbs of cheese after nibbling a box.
explanation.walkthrough: A jerrycan is a flat-sided metal fuel can, first used by German forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerrycan is a flat steel can for carrying petrol or water, so a type of container.

clue.text: Old car plant, almost the best of a bad bunch?

definitions.text: the best of a bad bunch?

parts.note: the Austin Maxi was a British car of the 1970s

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: mint is a garden herb, a plant

explanation.surface: A disused car factory is nearly the pick of a poor lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' reads as a factory for the old car, but it is the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: In game theory the maximin is the highest of the minimum outcomes: the least-bad choice among poor options.

clue.text: More obscene 20 getting caught

indicators.note: caught in the sense of heard: what is heard sounds like the cross-referenced word

parts.note: the answer to 20 Across, a shopkeeper

explanation.surface: Something lewder ends up being caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross can mean coarse or indecent, so the comparative is more indecent.

clue.text: Ballooning aristo ate no crackers

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so these letters go mad and are rearranged

explanation.surface: An aristocrat out in a balloon refused the crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits the aristo declined; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aerostation is the old term for the science or practice of flying lighter-than-air craft such as balloons.

clue.text: Maintain quiet aloofness

parts.note: P stands for piano, the musical direction for softly
reserve is a distant, restrained manner

explanation.surface: Keep up a silent, distant manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to keep it in its present state, a synonym of maintain.

clue.text: By George — adult lifting gear?

parts.note: via means by way of
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a grown-up raising machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting gear' suggests cranes and hoists, but the gear is something that helps a man rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Viagra is a drug taken to treat impotence, so humorously equipment for getting something up.

clue.text: Check out Orwell novel — see inside, you may use it for the time

definitions.text: you may use it for the time

indicators.note: inside says the single letter goes within the rearranged letters
novel means new, so the letters of the words before it are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: An invitation to look up a George Orwell book with an instruction to see inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orwell novel' reads as a book title, but 'novel' is the anagram signal for CHECK OUT plus ORWELL, and 'inside' puts V within the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A twelve-hour clock shows the time in two cycles of hours, morning and afternoon, so it is a way to read time.

clue.text: 1960s war film editor cutting one way to view 360?

indicators.note: the editor cuts into the phrase, sitting inside it

parts.note: 360 is thirty times twelve, so thirty dozen

explanation.surface: An editor trims a war movie from the 1960s, one way of watching it all round.
explanation.walkthrough: '360' suggests a full turn of view, but it is the number expressed as thirty dozen; ED goes in after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dirty Dozen is a 1967 Second World War film about twelve convicts sent on a mission.

clue.text: Tense, mostly annoyed, St Anthony is associated with this

definitions.text: St Anthony is associated with this

indicators.note: mostly means the final letter is left off

parts.note: taut means tight, tense
cross means angry, annoyed

explanation.surface: A tense, irritable state that a saint is linked with.
explanation.definitionFit: The T-shaped tau cross is also called St Anthony's cross, being the emblem of St Anthony the Great.

clue.text: Fail before limits of demand have subsided

indicators.note: before says the failing comes first in the answer

parts.note: to die is to stop working, to fail

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to own is to have

explanation.surface: Collapse before the limits of what is demanded have dropped away.
explanation.definitionFit: Died down means became less intense, as wind or noise lessens: a phrasal synonym of subsided.

clue.text: This will hopefully help one to get better still

definitions.text: This will hopefully help one to get better still

parts.words: This will hopefully help one to get better still
parts.note: a still is a photograph, and this camera lens gets a closer, better picture

explanation.surface: A remedy that one hopes will bring about further recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get better still' reads as getting even healthier, but a still is a single photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens with variable focal length lets a photographer close in on the subject for a better shot.

clue.text: Team quotes often hushed up after sacking wingers in squad

indicators.note: up in the sense of disturbed, so these letters are mixed
the letters dismissed must come out before the mixture gives the answer
the wingers of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A football club's comments are silenced after wide players are dropped from the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen of the South is a Scottish football club from Dumfries. The fodder holds the answer's letters plus S and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen of the South is a professional football club in Scotland, so a team.

clue.text: For one, 3 having complaint raised pitch

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Disraeli, answer to 3 Down, is one example of a PM, a prime minister
acne is a skin complaint

explanation.surface: A prime minister's grievance raised the tone.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch a tent is to set up camp, which is what encamp means.

clue.text: Error upset unknown heavenly model needing a wind-up?

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Y is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A mistake disturbs an unknown celestial model that must be cranked.
explanation.definitionFit: An orrery is a clockwork model of the solar system, often worked by a handle or key.

clue.text: Warning announced as plane possibly plummets

definitions.text: Warning announced as plane possibly plummets

parts.words: Warning announced as plane possibly plummets
parts.note: the plane is a plane tree, and the shout goes up as it is felled

explanation.surface: A crash alert given as an aircraft dives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' suggests an aircraft, but it is a plane tree, the London street tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumberjacks shout this word to warn others that a felled tree is about to crash down.

clue.text: Picked up 8 for food shop

indicators.note: picked up in the sense of heard, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: the answer to 8 Across, meaning more obscene

explanation.surface: Collected from the eighth item for a food shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Grocer here stands for the shop itself, as in 'going to the grocer's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer sells food and household goods; by metonymy the trader names the shop.

clue.text: Ex model, half drunk, leaving hotel

indicators.note: drunk means reeling, so these letters are thrown about
leaving says the letter for hotel departs from the word before

parts.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A former fashion model, half drunk, walks out of the hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half drunk' looks like a state of the model, but HALF is fodder, minus H, mixed with MODEL by 'drunk'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old flame is a former sweetheart, which is what an ex means in everyday speech.

clue.text: Stamp on letter, not a penny in old money abroad

indicators.note: not a means one copy of the next item is removed

parts.note: a postmark is the stamp printed over a letter's postage

explanation.surface: A letter's stamp is worth nothing in old foreign coinage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ostmark was the currency of East Germany, now defunct, so former foreign money.

clue.text: Bishop breaking wind died in a place of rest just like another?

definitions.text: a place of rest just like another?

indicators.note: the bishop breaks into the winding word, sitting inside it

parts.note: to twine is to wind round
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
D is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A bishop passing wind died and was laid in a resting place identical to the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' reads as flatulence, but it is the verb wind, TWINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Twin beds are a matching pair of single beds, each a sleeping place identical to the other.
